stumbles.quote: The two judges labelled 58 of those 63 as legitimate prose
stumbles.why: "The two judges" are never introduced (human reviewers? LLMs?). Also, "legitimate prose" is confusing: the cells are said to hold numbers and labels, not sentences, so it's unclear what was judged legitimate or whether the hits were false positives.

stumbles.quote: `--skip-quoted` already blanked table cells, but it also blanked blockquotes and italics.
stumbles.why: The text doesn't say this flag exists in the linter or how it is defined. It also doesn't explain why a new flag is needed instead of narrowing this one, though the next paragraph partly answers that.

stumbles.quote: a lint scan of 41 published posts reported 300 hits
stumbles.why: The text never explains what a "hit" is, meaning what the linter detects. The name `declaude_lint.py` and the "declauding" skill aren't explained either.

stumbles.quote: drafts that quote bad prose in italics on purpose
stumbles.why: It isn't clear what "bad prose" means or why italics mark it. This relies on an unstated convention of the declauding skill.

point: The PR adds a `--skip-tables` flag to the declaude linter that blanks lines starting with `|`, keeping line numbers intact. The aim is to cut false-positive hits in table cells without also skipping italics and blockquotes, as `--skip-quoted` does.
